turns.t: Good morning. Before we start, can I just check I've got the right person, Mrs. Oluwaseun Adeyemi-Clarke?
Yes. Yes, that's me. Though everyone just calls me Seun.
Seun it is. And who's come in with you today?
I'm Dilys, I'm her carer. I'm there every morning and most evenings, so she asked me to come along.
Lovely. Seun, are you happy for Dilys to stay in the room while we talk? Some of what we cover can be personal.
Oh, she knows all about it already. I'd, um... I'd rather she stayed, if that's all right.
Perfectly all right. So, what's brought you in today?
Well, it's a bit... it's embarrassing, really. It hurts when we try to be intimate. Me and my husband. And I...
Take your time. There's no hurry at all.
I just thought it would go away. But it hasn't, and now we've more or less stopped trying.
I'm sorry, that sounds like it's been hard on both of you. Can you tell me a bit more about the pain?
It's, well... at the start mostly. Sort of a burning, and then sore afterwards. I don't...
Burning at the start, and sore afterwards. Is that right?
Yes. That's it.
And do you remember roughly when that began?
It was... gosh. Around the, um...
It's been about six months now, doctor. She mentioned it to me around the time of the cold weather starting.
Yes, six months, that sounds right. It crept up on me.
Has anything else changed down there over those months? Any other symptoms you've noticed?
There's a dryness. I hadn't really thought it was connected, but it's there most of the time, even when we're not...
That's very useful to know. So the dryness is constant, and the pain with intercourse comes on at the start and lingers a little afterwards.
Yes, that's exactly what it's like.
Thank you for telling me, I know that wasn't easy. Now, let me ask about your general health. Any long-term conditions I should know about?
Only my blood pressure. High blood pressure, I've had it for years and years.
She takes the little tablet every morning, amlodipine. Five milligrams, I give it to her with her tea.
Good, that's one tablet, once a day, and it's the only medicine she takes?
That's the only one. I'd know, I do the pill organiser.
Perfect. And have you had any operations in the past, Seun?
I had a hysterectomy. About twelve years ago, it must be. They said it was fibroids.
Okay. And how are things at home generally? Who's around?
I live with my husband, but he isn't very steady on his feet now, so Dilys comes in to help the two of us. Nobody else, apart from my daughter on Sundays.
Right, I'd like to check a few measurements first, if you don't mind sitting still for me.
Of course. Do I need to take my cardigan off?
Just roll up the sleeve, please. Your blood pressure is 138 over 82.
Pulse is 72 beats per minute and regular.
Temperature is 36.7 degrees, and the oxygen level is 98 percent.
Is that good?
All perfectly fine. Your weight, from the scales in the corridor, was 64 kilograms, and breathing is 16 breaths a minute.
Now, with your permission, I'd like to examine you gently. Dilys, would you mind passing me that curtain?
Of course, doctor.
Thank you, Seun, that's all done and you can get dressed. The skin around the opening is thin and pale, and it looks dry, with a little redness but no sores or lumps.
Is it something serious? I was so worried it might be something nasty.
I don't see anything that worries me. Honestly, what you describe, together with the dryness and given your age, most likely points to thinning and dryness of the tissues from lack of oestrogen.
So it's the change, even this long after?
It can show up years later. It's my provisional thinking, and it's very treatable, so please don't feel embarrassed about it.
Will it need tablets, doctor? She's not keen on anything big.
We'll talk through gentle options at the next step. First I'd like a urine sample today, to rule out a water infection that could add to the burning. The nurse outside will give you a pot.
I can do that.
Good. In the meantime, go slowly, take your time and stop if it hurts, there's no pressure to try at all.
My husband is very understanding. It's me that's been... avoiding it.
That's very common, and nothing to feel guilty about.
And if it's still sore, doctor?
If it hasn't eased within a month, come back and see me and we'll go through the choices properly.
A month. Right, I'll write it on the calendar.
I'll remind her, don't you worry.
Wonderful. Thank you both for being so open with me today.
Thank you, doctor. That's a weight off.
